messages:
ci-bot: CI job `unit-tests / linux-py310` failed on main after merged lockfile update (#5123). failing test: tests/test_auth.py::test_token_refresh

ci-bot: Failure snippet:
```
> E   ImportError: cannot import name 'TokenV2' from 'authlib.tokens' (/workspace/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/authlib/tokens/__init__.py)
____________________________ test_token_refresh _____________________________
```
maya: I can reproduce locally after `git pull` + `poetry install` on macOS/py3.10. same ImportError.

samir: confirmed on linux container too. looks like a transitive bump in authlib or a subdep. #5123 touched poetry.lock only, right?

alejandro: yes, #5123 was lockfile refresh (ran `poetry lock` to pick newer transitive pins). can someone run `git show --pretty=oneline --name-only 5123` and grep the lock diff?

jen: quick check: `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- poetry.lock | grep authlib` shows authlib from 0.16.2 -> 0.17.0. that would explain TokenV2 removal.

patrick: okay that pins it down. options: revert the lockfile commit, pin authlib in pyproject (explicit dependency) or add a constraint in CI. thoughts? :thinking_face:

maya: revert is easiest short term (rollback lockfile to previous commit) and rerun CI to confirm no other breakages. but we should also decide whether to accept authlib 0.17 later and update code.

samir: can someone bisect the lockfile to be sure it's the authlib bump and not another change? bisecting a lockfile is awkward. easier: locally `poetry lock --no-update` to regenerate a lockfile consistent with pyproject (should keep constraints) — but since pyproject doesn't list authlib explicitly, it may still pick 0.17.

alejandro: alternative quick test: `poetry add authlib@0.16.2 --lock` to force the transitive pin and run tests. that doesn't need a lockfile revert, just ensures reproducible env.

jen: I kicked a rerun on the failed job with comment `ci rerun` (job: unit-tests/linux-py310).

ci-bot: Rerun started for job `unit-tests / linux-py310` (triggered by jen).

patrick: I'll open a quick PR pinning authlib==0.16.2 in pyproject.toml and regenerate poetry.lock. small delta, easier to review than full revert.

maya: TY. if the pin fixes CI we can follow-up with an issue to track upgrading to 0.17 and code changes.

samir: +1. also add a note in changelog/dep-updates so we don't surprise runtime behavior.

patrick: PR opened: #5134 — "pin authlib 0.16.2 to avoid import break after lock regen". Included lockfile regen. requesting review from eng-infra. :arrow_up_small:

ci-bot: PR #5134 triggered CI: unit-tests all jobs queued.

ci-bot: unit-tests/linux-py310 (PR #5134) — PASSED ✅

maya: green on my laptop too after `poetry install` from that PR. thanks Patrick.

jen: merging PR now. I'll add a follow-up task to track authlib upgrade and adjust tests.

ci-bot: Merged PR #5134 into main. Closing this thread as CI is green. :tada:

patrick: added issue #5135 to track upgrade to authlib 0.17 and required code changes.

maya: nice quick turnaround — good teamwork :thumbsup:
